newsitem.title: TAIWAN: First Taiwan ship departs for direct China sailing.
newsitem.headline: First Taiwan ship departs for direct China sailing.

text.p: The first ship to sail directly to communist China from Taiwan in 48 years departed from the island's southern Kaohsiung Harbour on Thursday.

"The Uni-Order just left the harbour," a port official said. The Uni-Order, registered in Panama and owned by Taiwan's Uniglory Marine Corp, was scheduled to arrive in China's Xiamen port early on Friday after a 12-hour voyage.

The voyage across the Strait is the first by a Taiwanese shipper since the Chinese civil war ended in 1949 with the communists in control of the Chinese mainland and the defeated Nationalists in exile on the island of Taiwan.
On Saturday the China-owned, Saint Vincent-registered Sheng Da ship sailed from Xiamen to Kaohsiung in the first direct voyage across the Taiwan Strait.
Taiwan, which has banned direct links with China since 1949, has agreed to allow limited direct shipping with the mainland under its "offshore transshipment centre" scheme.

Under the scheme, mainland cargoes are not allowed to enter Taiwan customs but can be transshipped at Kaohsiung for onward passage to third countries. Likewise, Taiwan cargoes at Kaohsiung cannot be put abroad ships planning to cross directly to the Chinese mainland.
